extracted.intended_audience: aspiring travel writers and memoirists; general creative writers
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for composing travel narratives and memoirs: what to include, how to interest readers, and common failings to avoid when describing places or an author's life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of travel writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Every writer of travels should consider, that, like all other authors, he undertakes either to instruct or please, or to mingle pleasure with instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you instruct, offer to the mind something to be imitated, or something to be avoided. If you please, offer new images to your reader and enable him to form a tacit comparison of his own state with that of others. Aim to either teach, entertain, or combine both purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid empty, detail-only itineraries
rubrics_metrics.description: Many travellers tell nothing because their method of travelling supplies them with nothing to be told — they record merely a sequence of places and trivial observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern examples to avoid: entering a town at night and judging it by the inn; listing hills, streams, rocks, and trees without meaning; catalogues of pictures, pillars, or pavement variegations; transcribing inscriptions or walls. Such minute enumerations leave no distinct idea and fail to instruct or please.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on human life and useful particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: He that would travel for the entertainment of others, should remember that the great object of remark is human life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report peculiarities of manufactures, works of genius, medicines, agriculture, customs, and policy. Be a useful traveller: bring home something that may benefit your country — a supply of want or mitigation of evil — so readers can compare and improve their own condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring back actionable or comparative insight
rubrics_metrics.description: The useful traveller procures some supply of want, or some mitigation of evil, which may enable his readers to compare their condition with that of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond pleasant images, provide readers with information they can use: technical practices, agricultural methods, medical remedies, or social/political observations that illuminate differences and suggest improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoir should emphasize distress and vicissitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing detains the reader's attention more powerfully than deep involutions of distress, or sudden vicissitudes of fortune.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing memoirs or an author's life, include episodes of deep trouble, sharp reversals, or sudden changes of fortune; these hold reader attention more than uniform, uneventful continuity. Show emotional stakes and turning points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure an author's life around works and public response
rubrics_metrics.description: The gradations of an author's life are from book to book. Every publication is a new period of time, from which some increase or declension of fame is to be reckoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize memoirs by significant publications, career milestones, and the social consequences (praise, invitations, coldness) that follow them; use these as narrative pivots to show progress, reputation, and changes in fortune.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify important terms; avoid ambiguous language
rubrics_metrics.description: The uncertainty and defects of language have produced very frequent complaints among the learned; yet there still remain many words among us undefined, which are very necessary to be rightly understood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define key words and concepts to prevent mischievous mistakes from erroneous interpretation. Precision of language helps readers understand distinctions (e.g., between similar social terms or moral qualities) and avoids confusion in argument or description.
